configuration.changes: New independent INT16 PE and testbench. Existing INT8/exact10 designs remain frozen. All modes use the same64-term array interface and exact int64 oracle.
configuration.conclusion: Compare complete32-bit product equality, DSP, LUT, FF, achieved II and clock. A one-DSP mixed implementation still spends LUT multipliers; integrate only after a demonstrated network budget.

estimates.basis: 64 independent pairs plus8-16 pipeline cycles; no internal frame memories. Direct16x16 uses one DSP per product. Byte-limb pairs use four27x9/8 DSP products. Overlap repair uses one27x16 DSP plus fabric8x16 and9x16 products; the mixed control uses one DSP plus fabric16x16. LUT/FF values reserve operand repair, carry chains, pipelining and array control; they are hypotheses, not primitive measurements.

configuration.interpretation: A complete signed16x16 product needs32 bits. Nonoverlapping two-product fields need at least gap32, making the coefficient port48 bits, beyond DSP48E2's27-bit input; splitting a coefficient alone leaves8x16 products needing24 bits and a32-bit packed port. P14 therefore splits both operands. P15 explicitly pays fabric recovery for overlapping fields. Count every DSP/fabric operation, compare P13/P16 controls, and retain failures or missed II without changing numerical gates.
configuration.name: int16_limb_packing
configuration.notes: PE only; two complete signed16 products per term, no network latency or Set14 claim
configuration.purpose: Split every signed16 value as unsigned low8 plus256*signed high8. Four packed byte-product pairs reconstruct both complete32-bit products exactly. Each low byte product fits a signed18 field, including unsigned255*255=65025. Expect four DSP48E2 multipliers per pair: exact generic16-bit limb packing alone loses DSP area versus two direct products.
